guides.favoredWhen: Tryndamere wins even-or-ahead duels by trading after her autos, dodging W with spin, and holding Ghost until Hookshot is spent; Camille wins if she kites with passive shields and escapes every all-in on E.

keyTips.text: Spin in right after she autos a minion, before the hit can trigger her shield. The trade starts while her passive is still dark, which is the only fair opening she gives.
keyTips.heading: Auto bait

keyTips.text: Keep exchanges short around her Q. Standing through repeated procs loses to the true-damage conversion, so hit and leave on every cycle.
keyTips.heading: Short trades

keyTips.text: Spend your spin to force or follow her Hookshot, never before it. Her E cooldown runs longer than yours, and a held Hookshot escapes both Ghost and your ultimate.
keyTips.heading: E for E

tips.text: Respect her level 1 and answer with short trades only. Neither side wins the opener by committing, so poke without overextending into her shield window.
tips.heading: Level-1 respect

tips.text: Check her summoners and runes before first contact. Her setups change the level-1 math completely, so scout the loadout before picking the opener.
tips.heading: Summoner scout

tips.text: Spin through her W instead of eating it, inward or out. Respect its range and slow for the whole lane, since the outer edge sets up everything she does next.
tips.heading: W dodge

tips.text: Bait the Hookshot with a re-engage threat before committing Ghost and R past level 6. She holds E to disengage exactly that combination, so force it out first.
tips.heading: Ghost bait

tips.text: Take the direct duel from even or ahead, and never donate free empowered Q hits on the way in. Your sustained damage holds the 1v1 once the approach is clean.
tips.heading: Even duel

tips.text: Ping the instant she leaves lane and check the sides. She roams even from behind, so answer the disappearance before her deficit becomes your team's problem.
tips.heading: Roam ping

keyTips.text: Tryndamere can pressure early, so look for aggressive trades and kills when the opponent gives an opening.
Treat Undying Rage as the commitment tool for a real all-in and save it for a window the matchup calls for rather than spending it before the fight matters.
In late game, punish an isolated or out-of-position enemy and use the resulting numbers advantage to take a major objective or tower.

tips.text: Build Fury through attacks; a full Fury bar improves his damage and the healing available through Bloodlust.
Keep the wave even or a little on your side when not already ahead, so the opponent has farther to retreat and you expose yourself less to ganks.
Use lane brush to hide the approach and surprise the opponent.
Use Bloodlust to recover after taking trade damage when that sustain helps you remain in lane.
His mobility and ultimate can help him stay on a target or escape, so save an all-in for a window when Undying Rage is ready if the matchup calls for it.
Apply split-push pressure around objective timers and challenge the enemy sent to answer you.
Take the duel when the responder is a favorable target; otherwise keep the side-lane pressure and make the enemy spend time answering.
Join the team when there is no useful objective-side split to create.
With more items, use his dueling strength to keep pressuring side lanes and draw a response.
If the enemy groups, group with the team; look for a flank toward an accessible squishy target while staying close enough to rejoin the allies.
Avoid entering a long front-to-back fight where the enemy can kite, disengage, or lock him down; those conditions blunt his access to targets.
Track Undying Rage availability: he is much easier to stop when the ultimate is down, so avoid forcing a risky fight in that window.

itemization.text: Take Hail of Blades, Sudden Impact, Grisly Mementos, and Treasure Hunter, plus Last Stand and Legend: Alacrity, adjusting if the matchup calls for another setup.
Build the popular item path of Ravenous Hydra, Berserker's Greaves, Phantom Dancer, Infinity Edge, and Lord Dominik's Regards.
Start Doran's Bow, a Health Potion, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Mortal Reminder as the alternative fourth item to Infinity Edge against substantial healing.
Keep Blade of the Ruined King, Guardian Angel, Death's Dance, Navori Flickerblade, and Mercurial Scimitar as situational choices, matching the defensive or anti-tank option to the opposing team.
Max Q, then E, then W, taking Undying Rage at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
